To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a 2-connected, non-complete graph with at least three vertices is pancyclic (with the exceptions of the 2-regular graph, and the 3-regular graph with at least 4 vertices), and that a 3-connected, non-complete, graph with at least four vertices is Hamiltonian connected.

the following conditions are necessary and sufficient for a 4-connected, 2-edge-connected, 2-connected, and 3-connected graph G to be Hamiltonian, pancyclic, and Hamiltonian-connected, respectively: (1) for each vertex x of G, the set of edges of G incident with x is the disjoint union of three paths of lengths 2 or 3; and (2) for each edge e of G, the graph G-e has a Hamiltonian path.

a 2-connected nontrivial graph G is pancyclic if and only if for every vertex v of G and every positive integer k, the number of vertices of degree k in G is less than or equal to k-1 times the number of vertices in G minus the number of vertices at distance at most 2 from v.
